evals.prompt: Rebase my local feature/payments branch onto origin/main. Keep the result local; do not push. Before changing anything, state the exact observations that govern the route.
evals.expected_output: The rebase skill takes the explicit start route, binds the named refs and safety state, and completes locally without publication.
assertions: Treats feature/payments as the source and origin/main as the target instead of guessing different refs.
Observes source and target OIDs, active-rebase state, worktree attachment, working-tree status, and worker ownership before mutation.
Starts replay only after the bound refs remain stable and the owning worktree is safe.
Verifies the requested history relationship and result ref after replay.
Does not push because publication was not authorized.

evals.prompt: Continue the rebase that is already active. The conflict resolution is staged in the worktree that owns the rebase metadata. Do not push.
evals.expected_output: The active lifecycle is recovered and continued in its owning worktree without starting a fresh rebase or publishing.
assertions: Rediscovers and binds the exact worktree and Git dir that own the active metadata.
Rebinds the remaining lifecycle contract and reobserves the same metadata immediately before continuing.
Uses the active-state continue route and never starts a fresh replay.
Verifies metadata and unmerged entries are absent before local completion.
Does not push because publication was not authorized.

evals.prompt: Abort the active rebase and restore the exact pre-rebase state, including the saved local work associated with this replay. Do not publish anything.
evals.expected_output: The active lifecycle is recovered, aborted in its owner, and restored to its bound pre-replay state.
assertions: Locates the metadata-owning worktree and binds the pre-replay OID before aborting.
Reobserves the active metadata and exact saved-entry identity immediately before mutation.
Aborts in the bound owner and verifies HEAD or the source ref equals the pre-replay OID.
Restores and drops only the uniquely bound saved entry after checks pass.
Performs no publication.

evals.prompt: Rebase feature/payments onto origin/main, then publish that same replay result to origin feature/payments. I authorize one force-with-lease push for this lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: Publication remains part of the explicitly authorized start lifecycle and uses an exact observed lease for one attempt.
assertions: Binds the publication remote, destination ref, initial destination OID, and one-attempt authority before replay.
Publishes only the verified result of this same start lifecycle after repository and interaction checks pass.
Fetches the exact destination before publication and reconciles compatible destination movement when required.
Uses force-with-lease tied to the final observed destination OID, never an unqualified force push.
Stops on lease rejection or later movement unless a new explicit decision and one-attempt authority are supplied.

evals.prompt: Merge origin/main into feature/payments so the branch contains the latest main commits.
evals.expected_output: The request is routed away from the rebase skill because it asks for a merge-based branch update.
assertions: Does not activate or execute the rebase workflow.
Identifies the requested operation as a merge-based update.
Does not rewrite local history or force-push.

evals.prompt: Configure our GitHub repository so pull requests allow rebase merging but disallow merge commits.
evals.expected_output: The request is routed to forge settings rather than local history replay.
assertions: Does not activate or execute the rebase workflow.
Recognizes repository merge-method configuration as forge administration.
Performs no local Git history mutation.

evals.prompt: Use GitHub's rebase-and-merge option to merge pull request 42.
evals.expected_output: The request is routed to pull-request merging rather than the local rebase skill.
assertions: Does not activate or execute the local rebase workflow.
Recognizes this as a forge pull-request merge action.
Does not run a local rebase or local force-push.

evals.prompt: The branch was rewritten earlier. Force-push its current tip to origin now; no rebase is active and I am not asking to start one.
evals.expected_output: The standalone publication request is routed away from the rebase skill.
assertions: Does not activate or execute the rebase workflow.
Recognizes that the request is push-only and outside a bound replay lifecycle.
Does not infer publication authority from an earlier unrelated rewrite.

evals.prompt: Continue my rebase. The current directory has no rebase metadata, but another linked worktree may own it and the original target name is missing from the handoff.
evals.expected_output: Recovery searches for the lifecycle owner, rebinds observable facts, and stops before mutation when the remaining contract is incomplete.
assertions: Searches linked worktrees and Git dirs for the exact active metadata owner.
Reports observed HEAD, refs, progress, unmerged entries, status, and saved-entry state from the owner.
Rebinds facts from current Git state and current task context without inventing the missing target.
Stops before continue or abort when the required target contract remains absent or inconsistent.

evals.prompt: Rebase my branch onto the latest branch and make the history look right.
evals.expected_output: Ambiguous source, target, and outcome stop the workflow before repository mutation.
assertions: Names the missing source ref, target ref, and observable result relationship.
Does not guess what 'my branch', 'latest branch', or 'look right' means.
Reports the supported alternatives and the facts needed to choose among them.
Performs no rebase, stash, worktree creation, ref update, or push.

evals.prompt: Continue the active rebase. The stopped commit and target both changed the same validation rule for different compatible reasons; preserve both intents if one tested resolution can do so.
evals.expected_output: Conflict handling traces both intents and selects a resolution only when exactly one tested outcome preserves all compatible intent.
assertions: Identifies the affected producers, consumers, interfaces, prompts, documentation, and observable behavior.
Enumerates semantic outcome classes and preserves every intent compatible with the bound replay goal.
Tests supported outcomes with repository-required and interaction-specific checks.
Continues only when exactly one staged outcome preserves compatible intent and passes checks.
Does not choose by ours/theirs labels, apparent recency, or side names.

evals.prompt: Rebase feature/payments onto origin/main. That branch is attached to another worktree where an automation worker is still writing, and the worker cannot currently acknowledge a pause.
evals.expected_output: Worktree and worker ownership prevent mutation until a safe checkpoint and handoff are observed.
assertions: Binds the exact attached worktree and Git dir instead of creating a competing worktree.
Requests a worker pause when supported and waits once for a checkpoint, end, or command result.
Performs no checkpoint, stash, replay, ref update, or push while the writer remains active or ownership is unknown.
Reports the last observed worker state and preserves the repository when no acknowledgement is observable.
Completes only after any acquired worker handoff obligation is acknowledged or the worker is observed stopped.

evals.prompt: Continue the rebase, but inspection confirms there is no active rebase metadata in the bound worktree or its Git dir.
evals.expected_output: The absent active lifecycle produces a read-only no-active-rebase result.
assertions: Confirms metadata absence in both the bound worktree and Git dir.
Reports that no active rebase exists and records the observation.
Does not start a fresh rebase in response to a continue request.
Performs no stash, worktree creation, ref update, commit, or push.
